info.title: Cardano Accounts API
info.description:
Read-only Cardano account data served from a [cardano-db-sync](https://github.com/IntersectMBO/cardano-db-sync) Postgres instance.

**Network:** `mainnet` (Cardano mainnet — stake addresses prefixed `stake1…`).

## Authentication

Every request under `/api/*` (except `/api/health`, `/api/info`, `/api/docs`, `/api/redoc`,
`/api/openapi.json`, the `/api/` landing page and `/api/signup`) must include a valid `x-project-id`
header (the legacy `project_id` header name is also accepted, but some proxies/CDNs on custom
domains silently strip headers with underscores — always prefer `x-project-id`):

- The public demo key is capped at 50 requests/hour per source IP.
- Any other key is validated against a database of issued keys and their status.
- Missing or invalid keys get `401`; a demo key over its hourly cap gets `429`.

```
curl -H "x-project-id: YOUR_KEY" \
  https://<host>/api/accounts/stake1ux...
```

## Concepts

- All amounts are Lovelace (1 ADA = 1 000 000 Lovelace), returned as strings.
- All time fields are UNIX timestamps in seconds.
- Addresses, stake addresses and pool IDs are bech32.
- Pagination on list endpoints: `count` (1–100, default 100), `page` (default 1), `order` (`asc`|`desc`, default `asc`).

## Response conventions

These rules hold across the whole API and are the first thing an automated client should know.

- **Amounts are strings.** Lovelace amounts (ADA × 1 000 000), token quantities, stake and voting power are returned as
  decimal strings so they cannot lose precision. Parse them as big integers, never as floats. Ratios are separate
  `numerator`/`denominator` pairs or plain numbers where a field says so.
- **Times are UNIX seconds** (`block_time`, `time`, `*_time`). Epochs are integer epoch numbers; one epoch is 5 days.
- **Identifiers.** Block and transaction hashes are lower-case 64-character hex. Stake addresses start with `stake1`,
  payment addresses with `addr1`, pools with `pool1`, DReps with `drep1`/`drep_script1` (CIP-129 and CIP-105 forms are accepted
  where a path parameter says so). A native asset `unit` is the policy id (56 hex) followed by the hex asset name.
- **`null` means "not applicable or unknown"**, never zero. A field that is absent for one record type is `null` or omitted.
- **Lists** use `count` (1–100), `page` (1-based) and `order` (`asc`|`desc`). A page past the end returns `200` with `[]`.
  Most list endpoints return a bare JSON array and no total; request the next page until a short or empty page is returned.
- **Data is read live from cardano-db-sync** and trails the chain tip by seconds. Use `/api/health` (`tip_block`) or
  `/api/blocks/latest` to see how current the data is.
- **Heuristic and estimated fields are labelled.** Responses that are model-derived carry flags such as `estimate: true`
  or `heuristic: true`; do not treat them as ledger facts.

## Errors

Every non-2xx response is a flat JSON object `{"status_code": 404, "error": "Not Found", "message": "..."}`
(`ErrorResponse`). Typical codes: `400` malformed identifier or parameter; `401` missing/invalid key; `404` the
address, hash, pool, epoch or asset does not exist in the indexed chain; `422` a parameter is outside its allowed range;
`429` rate limit exceeded (honour `Retry-After`); `500`/`503`/`504` transient server or database problems, safe to retry
with back-off. Rate-limit state is returned in the `X-RateLimit-*` response headers.

Decoded metadata for any valid address on this network, used or not.

Unlike the other address routes this answers 200 for a valid address that
has never appeared on-chain. `used` is true/false from the indexed
`tx_out` lookup, or null when the address is too long for that index

`stake_credential` is decoded from the address itself (base addresses
only). It identifies the delegation part, not the address owner: anyone
can build an address with any stake credential. `stake_address` is the
value db-sync recorded on-chain when the address has been used

decoded one (`"address"`), otherwise null.

entries or locks.

the requested recipients and amounts, the recorded lifecycle, and the
payouts db-sync observed.

`payout_verification.status`: `verified` (every payout group's recorded
total and count equal what its enacted proposals requested),
`partially_observed` (some groups verified, others not observed),
`not_observed` (db-sync has processed the enactment boundary but
recorded no payout — not proof the ledger didn't pay), `mismatch`
(payouts recorded but the amounts — compared as sorted multisets, so
totals and counts too — or the earned epochs differ; `mismatch_reasons`),
`pending` (not enacted yet), `not_applicable` (expired or dropped),
`unavailable` (the enactment boundary isn't recorded yet, even if some
payouts are, or data is missing; `partial`).

A group is every enacted proposal paying one recipient at one epoch.
`attribution.level`: `proposal` (each payment's group has this proposal
alone), `group_only` (verified only as a group — never split between
its proposals, nor matched by amount, equal or not), `partial`, `none`.

Lovelace amounts are exact strings. `treasury_context` (ada_pots) is
context only: the treasury's change includes other inflows.
